messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for customer 'Sable Retail' on Dedicated cluster 'dedicated-sable-us-west2'. Error spike started ~4750012300. Alert: dedicated.gateway.5xx_rate > 5% for 5m. Severity: P1.

oncall-aaron: I'm on it. Can someone drop the dashboard and top metrics?

sre-amber: dashboards -> https://dash.re/redwood/dedicated/sable-us-west2 (logs + per-tenant throughput). Quick peek: 502/504 + a bunch of 524 gateway timeouts. Error rate jumped to ~12% at peak.

eng-runtime-zoe: seeing long tail on token generation time, big headroom on CPU but GPU queues are full. Could be KV-store thrash causing backpressure into runtime.

infra-miguel: kubectl top nodes shows one host at 98% memory and iowait creeping. Not typical for model kernels — likely noisy tenant using large batch sizes.

support-jake: CS got multiple reports from Sable: "time outs during checkout personalization", started ~14:05 PDT. They report 15% of requests failing from our side.

oncall-aaron: ok action plan: 1) identify noisy tenant(s) 2) apply short-term throttle/evict 3) scale burst capacity if possible 4) route critical Sable traffic to fallback model/hosted. Assigning Amber + Zoe + Miguel.

sre-amber: running tenant query now: `SELECT tenant_id, p99_latency, inflight_reqs FROM metrics.tenants WHERE cluster='dedicated-sable-us-west2' ORDER BY inflight_reqs DESC LIMIT 10;`

sre-amber: result (snip):
```
tenant_id   | p99_latency | inflight_reqs
noisy-tenant-77 | 7.8s        | 1,200
sable-retail     | 2.1s        | 300
other-tenant-9   | 0.5s        | 50
```

eng-runtime-zoe: noisy-tenant-77 is using continuous long-context streaming with very large batch requests. It’s eating KV cache and blocking qps.

infra-miguel: eviction candidates: 1) throttle by weight 2) graceful eviction to smaller instance 3) full tenant eviction (last resort). We can push a transient throttle via routectl: `routectl set-weight noisy-tenant-77 0.2 --cluster dedicated-sable-us-west2`

support-jake: Sable CS: are they impacted by noisy-tenant-77 specifically? CS asked for ETA and mitigation steps they can surface to customer.

cs-lena: Confirmed — Sable's errors correlate with the time noisy-tenant-77 ramped up. I'll notify Sable that we're mitigating and may shift them to a fallback model if needed.

oncall-aaron: Amber/Miguel, please apply throttle. Zoe, prepare a rollback route to `quantized-compact-v1` hosted fallback and ensure keys/telemetry preserved.

eng-runtime-zoe: preparing route: `redwood route update --from tenant=sable-retail --to model=quantized-compact-v1 --preserve-headers --reason "failover during cluster saturation"` will take ~90s to warm. Also prepping a canary with 10% traffic.

sre-amber: Throttle applied: `routectl set-weight noisy-tenant-77 0.15` — confirming backend queues dropping.

infra-miguel: Just evicted one pod replicaset running noisy-tenant-77 workloads; autoscaler triggered and created extra pods but queue length reduced. I also bumped burst pool by +2 GPU nodes (reserved burst), coords with Dedicated autoscale policy.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation actions logged: throttle noisy-tenant-77, evict pod X, +2 burst nodes added, route canary for Sable to quantized-compact-v1.

oncall-aaron: Monitoring error rate now. Amber — can you post a short logs snippet showing 5xx before/after?

sre-amber: logs (before):
```
[2026-03-15T14:07:12Z] tenant=noisy-tenant-77 request_id=abcd status=502 backend_err="kv: eviction in progress" latency=6.2s
[2026-03-15T14:08:03Z] tenant=sable-retail request_id=efgh status=524 gateway_timeout latency=10.1s
```
After ~6m:
```
[2026-03-15T14:14:30Z] tenant=noisy-tenant-77 request_id=ijkl status=200 latency=0.9s
[2026-03-15T14:14:31Z] tenant=sable-retail request_id=mnop status=200 latency=0.7s
```

support-jake: CS notified Sable with an interim message: "We're throttling a noisy tenant and routing a portion of your traffic to a compact fallback; expect reduced errors within ~10 minutes." Sable support asked for postmortem.

cs-lena: Sable acknowledged. They asked about perf delta on fallback model — estimated 8–12% slower but stable. They're fine with temporary fallback.

infra-miguel: Metrics trending down: cluster 5xx from 12% -> 1.8% over 9 minutes. GPU queue depth down from 1,900 -> 420. KV eviction rate normalized.

oncall-aaron: Great. Next: keep throttles for 30m, keep burst nodes for 1h, open an incident ticket for follow-up with Eng Runtime and CS. Amber, Zoe — please add remediation actions.

eng-runtime-zoe: Opening follow-up ticket: `INC-4750012345` assigned to eng-runtime. Actions: 1) improve tenant-level backpressure (short-term throttle automation) 2) KV cache isolation per-tenant (medium) 3) refine autoscaler thresholds to preemptive burst.

sre-amber: Post-incident checklist: 1) reconcile billing for burst nodes used 2) review noisy-tenant-77 quota enforcement 3) add more granular alert: dedicated.cluster.queue_depth per-tenant 4) run a load-replay test for noisy-tenant-77 pattern.

support-jake: I'll coordinate customer comms and schedule a follow-up with Sable for RCA next week.

cs-lena: Noted. They want a timeline for permanent mitigations; we'll include eng ETA in the RCA.

oncall-aaron: Declaring incident as mitigated at 4750012740 — error rates back to baseline and Sable on fallback canary. Leaving throttles in place until follow-up. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated. Created incident record INC-4750012345 and scheduled postmortem.

eng-runtime-zoe: quick note — saved relevant logs and KV diagnostics to /var/logs/incidents/INC-4750012345.tar.gz for the postmortem. Will attach perf numbers.

infra-miguel: Follow-up ops: consider hard cap on inflight_reqs per-tenant to prevent single tenant from exhausting kv/gpu caches. Filing infra action item.

sre-amber: I'll add the alert tuning and owner to the ticket.

support-jake: Closing loop with CS after RCA draft.

oncall-aaron: Good job team. We'll review timeline in postmortem — assign owners and due dates there.
